work.label: SELECTED WORK
work.intro1: A short list of platforms I've shipped end-to-end —
work.introEmph: from API design and database schemas to AWS infrastructure and CI/CD.

mie.name: Make it in the Emirates — Awards Platform
mie.blurb: Government platform for the UAE Ministry of Industry & Advanced Technology. End-to-end ownership across frontend, backend, infra, and CI/CD.

caseStudy.problem: Deliver a public-facing awards platform for the UAE Ministry of Industry & Advanced Technology — concurrent traffic from applicants, jurors, and program operators, with the security and uptime expectations of a government deployment.
caseStudy.architecture: Next.js frontend and NestJS backend over PostgreSQL with Prisma. AWS infrastructure across VPC, EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFront, ECS, and CodePipeline. Container-based deploys, Vitest + Playwright for unit/E2E coverage, structured logging into CloudWatch.
caseStudy.contributions: Owned the frontend architecture, API surface, database schema, and AWS infra end-to-end. · Rewrote the deployment pipeline around containers + CodePipeline, taking releases from 20 minutes to under five. · Optimised PostgreSQL queries and added a targeted caching layer that cut median API latency by 35%. · Introduced structured logging + dashboards that reduced mean time to issue detection by ~40%.

sabeel.name: Sabeel — Mobile Backend
sabeel.blurb: Backend powering a high-traffic mobile product. Hardened the API surface, cut latency, and shipped reliable infra on AWS.

caseStudy.problem: A growing mobile app needed a backend that could handle thousands of concurrent users without latency spikes, plus a deploy pipeline the team could trust.
caseStudy.architecture: Laravel API on AWS ECS behind an ALB, MySQL on RDS, static assets through S3 + CloudFront. CI/CD pushing through ECR with CloudWatch monitoring and alerts.
caseStudy.contributions: Profiled and refactored the hottest endpoints, dropping median latency by ~30%. · Containerised the API and moved deployments onto ECS for predictable rollouts. · Hardened auth, role-based access, and request validation across the API surface. · Set up CloudWatch dashboards and alarms so on-call could spot regressions in minutes.

esl.name: Egyptian Schools League — Competition Engine
esl.blurb: Modular competition engine with real-time leaderboards. Replaced spreadsheet workflows with a configurable rules engine.

caseStudy.problem: Operators were running national school competitions out of spreadsheets — slow scoring, fragile state, and no real-time visibility for participants.
caseStudy.architecture: Next.js front-end, NestJS back-end with a modular rules engine, PostgreSQL via Prisma, and a Docker-based deploy. WebSockets for live leaderboard updates.
caseStudy.contributions: Designed the rules-engine abstraction so new competition formats are config, not code. · Built the real-time leaderboard pipeline and the operator dashboards that consume it. · Reduced manual admin work by ~80% by replacing spreadsheet ingest with structured forms + validation.

wabot.name: WhatsApp AI Chatbot Automation
wabot.blurb: Serverless AI chatbot combining Amazon Lex and Twilio to automate customer-support workflows on WhatsApp.

caseStudy.problem: Support agents were drowning in repetitive WhatsApp inquiries — order status, hours, common FAQs — and customers waited hours for answers any bot could give in seconds.
caseStudy.architecture: Twilio webhook → AWS Lambda (Python) → Amazon Lex for intent + slot filling, with secrets in AWS Secrets Manager and CloudWatch for traceability. Pure event-driven: scales to zero between conversations.
caseStudy.contributions: Designed intent + slot taxonomy across the support team's real ticket history. · Wrote the Lambda orchestration that bridges Lex, Twilio, and the internal CRM. · Automated ~60% of inbound conversations end-to-end, escalating cleanly to a human when confidence dropped.

eltan.name: Eltanfeethi — Azure Delivery
eltan.blurb: Led Azure infrastructure, release pipelines, and production deployment for a managed government-services platform.

caseStudy.problem: A managed government-services platform needed Azure infra stood up, API gateway in place, and a release process the team could actually trust before going to production.
caseStudy.architecture: Azure compute + storage, Azure API Management fronting the service surface, release pipelines through Azure DevOps with environment gates.
caseStudy.contributions: Designed the Azure infrastructure layout — subscriptions, network, identity, and policy. · Configured API Management with the routing, throttling, and key-management the platform required. · Built the release pipelines and gates that took the platform from staging into a production rollout.

r1.b1: Architecting and shipping the UAE Ministry of Industry & Advanced Technology awards platform serving 2,000+ concurrent users.
r1.b2: Owning frontend (Next.js), backend (NestJS), PostgreSQL schema design, and AWS infrastructure end-to-end.
r1.b3: Cut deployment time from 20min → <5min and reduced API latency by 35% through container-based CI/CD and query optimization.

r2.b1: ~1,200 hours of full-stack engineering training across the MERN, .NET, and cloud tracks.
r2.b2: Capstone projects covered API design, container deployment, and infrastructure automation.

r3.b1: Delivered React / Next.js applications for clients across e-commerce, education, and SaaS.
r3.b2: Owned the full delivery loop: design handoff → implementation → deployment → maintenance.
